title: Evaluating LLM Adaptation to Sociodemographic Factors: User Profile vs. Dialogue History

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the Jensen-Shannon divergence in the probability distributions of LLM responses to Hofstede's Value Survey Module (VSM 2013) questions when users are grouped by varying 10-year age brackets, provided either explicitly in a profile or implicitly via dialogue history.
Comparing the divergence of model responses to value survey questions across different user educational attainment levels (e.g., high school vs. doctoral degrees) to quantify value adaptation.

Grouping LLM responses to the value survey by job categories and hierarchical position levels (e.g., Entry Level vs. C-Suite) derived from zero-shot classification of user job titles to assess behavioral divergence.

Evaluating shifts in expressed cultural and social values by categorizing the simulated user's country of origin into economic development levels (Developed, Developing, Third World) and measuring inter-group response divergence.
